text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Ceasefire in Freetown fighting as African leaders endorse bombardment of the city by Nigerian-led West African force to restore democratic government ousted by soldiers in a coup.
- Task force on petrol to meet on Thursday to find lasting solution to persistent fuel shortage in the country.
- Scarcity of loanable funds is imminent as government's tight monetary squeeze hits banks.
- Nigerian stock exchange capitalisation hits 360 billion naira in first quarter of 1997, a 28.68 percent increase from the corresponding period last year.

- Goodie Ibru, a lawyer and leading businessman, is elected chairman of Nigerian stock exchange, succeeding Pascal Dozie, chief executive of Diamond Bank, who has held the post for the past three years.
- Government denies claim that 300 Nigerian soldiers are being held hostage in on-going confrontation in Sierra Leone to reinstate ousted civilian government.
- Police warn against any rallies on June 12 to mark fourth anniversary of annulled presidential election.
- Foreign minister Tom Ikimi says Nigeria will not look back in bid to restore ousted democratic government in Sierra Leone.
- Industrialists shun export processing zone in Calabar, southeastern Nigeria because of high costs.
